description: A suburban hotel on Fay Avenue that has been trading since 1967 under the line "your local since 1967". Facilities include a bar, bistro open daily for lunch and dinner, TAB, a VIP lounge, multiple beer gardens and a children's playground. The venue caters for functions from casual gatherings to formal events and runs a loyalty membership program.
highlights: Bistro open daily for lunch and dinner

name: Turvey Park Hotel
description: A renovated local pub on Bolger Avenue with a courtyard, dining room and betting lounge. The bistro serves lunch and dinner daily with weekday lunch specials and nightly dinner deals, and there is a drive-through bottle shop. Live music plays on weekends and the venue takes function bookings.
highlights: Courtyard, dining room and betting lounge
Weekday lunch specials and nightly dinner deals

name: Ashmont Inn Hotel
description: A recently renovated, family friendly hotel on Tobruk Street in Ashmont, close to the Pomingalarna bicycle park. It serves food and drinks and has an attached bottle shop. Trading is 10am to midnight Monday to Saturday and 10am to 10pm Sunday.

name: Rules Club Wagga
description: A large licensed club on Fernleigh Road with a bistro serving wood-fired pizzas, a cafe, a sports bar, a gaming room and multiple function rooms including a boardroom and bridal room. Outside there are bowling greens with barefoot bowls, a sports oval, netball courts and tennis courts. A courtesy bus runs, the club holds bingo and raffles, and the adjoining 79-room Quality Hotel provides accommodation with secure parking.
highlights: Bistro with wood-fired pizzas and a cafe
Sports oval, netball and tennis courts

name: The Blamey Hotel
description: A family friendly pub and bistro on Main Street at Lake Albert with a free courtesy bus. The bistro serves lunch and dinner daily, sport plays on large screens, and there is a bottle shop with a delivery service. Live entertainment runs Friday and Saturday evenings, and the venue has gaming and TAB plus function space.

name: Wagga Wagga Country Club
description: A golf club on Plumpton Road set along the banks of Lake Albert, with an 18-hole championship course of 6,054 metres off the back markers, bent greens and all-weather fairways. The clubhouse holds the Lakeview Eatery, open for lunch and dinner, and a pro shop offering equipment and coaching. Function facilities cater for up to 200 people and the club offers golf memberships and reciprocal club access.
highlights: Lakeview Eatery for lunch and dinner
18-hole championship course of 6054 metres from the back markers
On the shores of Lake Albert

name: Uranquinty Hotel
description: A village pub on Morgan Street at Uranquinty, open Monday to Sunday from midday. It has a public bar with TAB and gaming machines, a bottle shop with takeaway, and bistro meals for dine-in or takeaway Wednesday to Sunday. The pub runs a courtesy bus, offers free camping and a children's play area, and displays historical memorabilia, with regular raffles and pub draws through the week.
highlights: Public bar with TAB and gaming machines
Bistro meals Wednesday to Sunday, dine-in or takeaway

name: Junee Hotel
description: A heritage country hotel on Seignior Street, trading since 1878 when it opened as the Railway Hotel, with Federation Filigree and Art Nouveau detailing. The kitchen serves lunch from midday and dinner from 6pm using Riverina produce, and there is a bar, beer garden and bottle shop. Heritage guest rooms are available upstairs, dogs are welcome in the outdoor areas, and the hotel takes function bookings.
highlights: Operating since 1878, originally the Railway Hotel
Federation Filigree and Art Nouveau building
Lunch and dinner using Riverina produce

name: Criterion Hotel Gundagai
description: A Sheridan Street pub in Gundagai whose bar carries original oil-painted murals depicting bushrangers and the 1852 flood. Meals and pizzas are served seven nights a week in a family friendly setting. The hotel has King Single, Queen and Family accommodation rooms, and runs live music, happy hour, pool competitions and sport on screen.
highlights: Bar with original oil-painted historical murals
King Single, Queen and Family rooms

name: Narrandera Ex-Servicemen's Club
description: A licensed club on Bolton Street in Narrandera describing itself as a venue for dining, entertainment and community. The Riverina Wok N Grill restaurant operates on site alongside the bar. The club runs weekly raffles, member badge draws, live entertainment, social dancing classes, trivia, bingo and poker, and takes function bookings.
highlights: Riverina Wok N Grill restaurant on site
Weekly raffles and member badge draws

name: Coolamon Hotel
description: A historic pub on Cowabbie Street in Coolamon, established in 1880, split into several distinct spaces: The Garden outdoor bar, The Dining Room, The Front Bar for cocktails and casual drinks, The Glasshouse covered dining area, The Lounge and The Long Room for functions. The pub is open daily from 11.30am with the kitchen running 11.30am to 2.30pm and 5.30pm to 8.30pm, and pizza available seven days. Accommodation, weddings, functions and online ordering are all offered.
highlights: The Long Room for functions and weddings

name: The Rock Memorial Bowling Club
description: A lawn bowls club on Urana Street at The Rock that has been operating since 1939. Dining is at Crystal's Restaurant with an Australian menu, and there is a bar alongside the greens. The club programs live music, bingo and trivia nights, and offers membership with discounts and access to club events.

name: Culcairn Hotel
description: A country hotel on Railway Parade in Culcairn offering budget accommodation in Queen, Single, Twin Share and Family rooms, all with shared bathrooms upstairs and flat-screen smart TVs. The venue also runs a bistro, a beer garden and a playground. Extended stay discounts are available and accommodation reception is closed on Christmas Day.
highlights: Budget pub accommodation with shared bathrooms
Queen, Single, Twin Share and Family rooms

name: Holbrook Returned Servicemen's Club
description: A returned servicemen's club on Swift Street in Holbrook with a restaurant, bar, and Keno and TAB betting. The club takes in a golf club and a bowls club, along with boating and angling sections. It offers memberships and hosts functions, trading 10am to 9pm Saturday to Thursday and until 10.30pm on Friday.

name: Bush & Campbell
description: Accounting and advisory firm at 30 Blake Street in central Wagga Wagga. The practice lists taxation and accounting, business advisory services, succession planning, CFO services, financial planning, audit and assurance, and self managed superannuation. Alongside the Wagga Wagga office the firm also has offices at Lockhart, Tumbarumba and Tumut.
highlights: Taxation and accounting for individuals and businesses
Also has Lockhart, Tumbarumba and Tumut offices

name: WDF Accounting + Advisory
description: Accounting and advisory practice at 135-137 Peter Street, Wagga Wagga. Service lines listed on their site are tax and compliance, business advisory, superannuation, smart accounting, bookkeeping and payroll, and an HR partner service. The office is open weekdays from 8:30am to 5:00pm.
highlights: Tax and compliance work for businesses and individuals

name: Farrell Lusher Solicitors
description: Law firm at 39 Fitzmaurice Street that has practised in Wagga Wagga since 1910. Areas of work listed are family law including divorce, property settlements and parenting orders, criminal and driving matters, wills and estates, conveyancing, personal injury litigation and commercial law. Reception is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm.
highlights: Family law, divorce and parenting matters
Criminal law, AVOs and driving offences
Wills, probate and powers of attorney

name: Tankard's Law
description: Criminal and traffic law practice in Shop 6 at 54 Fitzmaurice Street, Wagga Wagga. The firm's listed work covers drug offences, assaults, break and enter, fraud and firearms matters on the criminal side, and drink driving, drug driving, speeding, dangerous driving, licence appeals and heavy vehicle offences on the traffic side.
highlights: Fitzmaurice Street office in the CBD

name: Bower Wood Lawyers
description: Law firm at 57 Gurwood Street, Wagga Wagga, with a second office at 54 The Parade, Tumbarumba. The practice works in business and commercial law, conveyancing and property development, and estate planning and administration.

name: Fitzpatricks Real Estate
description: Real estate agency on Baylis Street in the Wagga Wagga CBD. The agency handles residential sales and rentals, commercial property, property management, rural property and land sales, and offers free property appraisals along with maintenance request and e-alert services for owners and tenants.
highlights: Property management with online maintenance requests

name: Kitson Property
description: Wagga Wagga real estate agency at 66 Baylis Street handling sales, leasing and property management. The agency provides sales appraisals, investment advice, tenant forms and an online maintenance request system for renters.

name: Ray White Wagga Wagga
description: Real estate office at 83 Morgan Street covering residential, land, commercial and rural sales plus rentals and property management. The office states it has been part of the Wagga real estate industry for over 30 years and also operates offices at Junee and Coolamon. Free in-person and desktop appraisals are offered.
highlights: Also operates Junee and Coolamon offices

name: Paper Plane Finance
description: Mortgage broking business listed on Baylis Street, Wagga Wagga. The broker works across home loans, investment loans and refinancing, assisting first home buyers, repeat purchasers and property investors.

name: Angry Ant Web Design
description: Web and design studio with offices in Wagga Wagga and the Shoalhaven. Services listed are web design, branding, graphic design and social media, with client work described across government, tourism, medical, hospitality, festival and agricultural sectors.
highlights: Offices in Wagga Wagga and the Shoalhaven

name: Quickprint Wagga
description: Printing business on Fitzmaurice Street covering business stationery, promotional items, design, event and wedding printing, signage and labels. The shop trades weekdays from 8:30am to 4:30pm and is closed on weekends.

name: Khan Signs
description: Locally owned signage business on Pearson Street that describes servicing Wagga and Australia for over 30 years. Work covers vehicle signage and wraps, fleet branding, illuminated and 3D lettering, shopfront and reception signage, safety and wayfinding signs, large format and digital printing, laser cutting and engraving, and paint protection film. The business is a 3M Select partner.

name: Best St. Dental
description: Dental practice at 122 Best Street offering family and preventive dentistry, cosmetic and smile design work, orthodontics, dental implants, root canal treatment, periodontal treatment and hygiene, teeth whitening, sleep apnoea and snoring treatment, and emergency appointments. The practice offers CEREC same-day crowns and is open weekdays from 8am to 5pm.
highlights: Dental implants and root canal treatment

name: Shumack Dental & Implants
description: Dental practice on Trail Street covering family dentistry, restorative work such as fillings, crowns, bridges, dentures and veneers, and single and full arch dental implants. The practice also lists periodontics, sleep dentistry, orthodontics, mouthguards, a mobile dentistry service and same-day emergency appointments. It opens weekdays 8am to 5pm and every second Saturday morning.
highlights: Single and full arch dental implants

name: Wagga Physiotherapy and Sports Injury Centre
description: Physiotherapy and sports injury rehabilitation practice at 45 Best Street. The centre states it has been operating for over 30 years and works alongside general practitioners, specialists, gyms and local sporting groups.
highlights: Works with GPs, specialists and sporting clubs

name: Body Dynamics Health
description: Allied health clinic on Kincaid Street combining physiotherapy with exercise physiology and dietetics. The clinic runs an onsite exercise clinic, the Beat It diabetes program and sports performance consulting.

name: Granger Chiropractic
description: Chiropractic clinic at 67 Johnston Street treating neck pain and headaches, arthritis and sports injuries, with care for families and children. Techniques listed include the Activator Method, Diversified Technique, Sacral Occipital Technique and the Thompson Technique. The practice is a member of the Australian Chiropractors Association.
highlights: Activator, Diversified, SOT and Thompson techniques

name: Lightfoot Podiatry
description: Locally owned podiatry clinic in the D'Hudson Arcade on Baylis Street. Treatments listed are general toenail care, corns and calluses, ingrown toenail removal using the BS Brace, advice on tinea and other foot infections, and diabetic foot assessments and complications. The clinic is on the ground floor for disability access and is Department of Veterans Affairs approved. It consults Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 9am to 4pm.
addressLine: Shop 6, Ground Floor, D'Hudson Arcade, 176-178 Baylis Street
highlights: General toenail, corn and callus care
Ingrown toenail treatment with BS Brace
Ground floor arcade location with disability access

name: Zacharia Naumann Optometry
description: Independent optometry practice at 210 Baylis Street. Services include comprehensive eye examinations, children's vision assessments, myopia control and orthokeratology, dry eye treatment, computer vision care and emergency eye care. The dispensary carries frames, sunglasses, contact lenses, sports eyewear, safety specs and Rodenstock DNEye biometric lenses. Late consultations run on Thursdays and the practice opens Saturday mornings.
highlights: Frames, contact lenses, sports and safety eyewear

name: Lake Road Veterinary Hospital
description: Veterinary hospital on Lake Albert Road that states it is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Services listed include consultations, diagnostics, advanced medical care, rehabilitation, grooming, puppy preschool, wildlife care and referral support for other veterinary practices.
highlights: Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year

name: Kooringal Vet Hospital
description: Veterinary hospital at 2 Kimberley Drive, Tatton. Healthcare services include vaccinations, health checks, microchipping, radiography, ultrasonography and parasite control, while surgical work covers dental, desexing, ophthalmology, orthopaedic, soft tissue and emergency procedures. The clinic also offers behavioural advice, grooming, nutrition guidance, puppy preschool and rabbit and reptile care, and lists a 24 hour emergency service.
highlights: Dental, orthopaedic and soft tissue surgery

name: Michael O'Reilly Pharmacy
description: Pharmacy at 67 Baylis Street in the Wagga Wagga CBD. Services listed are PBS, concession and DVA dispensing, vaccinations including flu, whooping cough, MMR and COVID-19, sleep apnoea consultations and equipment, weekly medicines packs, MedsChecks, blood pressure and blood glucose monitoring, bowel cancer screening, baby weighing and absence from work certificates. Scripts can be uploaded online and appointments booked through the site.

name: Southcity Community Pharmacy
description: Pharmacy in the South City Shopping Centre on Tanda Place. The pharmacy offers Webster packing, custom compounding, online prescriptions and delivery, vaccinations, sleep apnoea support, pharmacist consultations and Farm Door frozen meals. It trades seven days, 8am to 7pm on weekdays and 9am to 5pm on weekends.
addressLine: Shop 5A, South City Shopping Centre, 1-7 Tanda Place

name: Lulu & Kit Haircutters
description: Fitzmaurice Street salon doing men's and women's cutting, colour work including highlights, foils, balayage, freehand placement, colour correction and toning, plus blow drying, curls, straightening and wedding and event styling. Treatments include O&M and Christophe Robin ranges, and the salon stocks Kevin Murphy, Eleven, O&M, GHD, Cloud Nine, Redken and K18. Late night trading on Thursdays.
highlights: Stocks Kevin Murphy, Eleven, O&M and K18

name: Plush Hairdressing
description: Salon at 9 Trail Street offering precision cutting, bespoke colour including lightening and toning, blow-outs and special occasion styling, bridal work, and scalp and smoothing treatments with hair and scalp analysis. Bookings are taken through Fresha and the salon sells take-home hair care products.

name: Big Barber Delux
description: Barber shop in Sturt Mall on Baylis Street, one of two Big Barber Delux shops in Wagga Wagga alongside the Marketplace store. The barbers do men's, seniors' and boys' haircuts, beard trims and styling, wet shaves and hair tattoos, and sell hair and beard care products. No appointment is needed and walk-ins are welcome.

name: BY KIRRA Skin & Beauty
description: Skin and beauty studio at 105 Forsyth Street offering facials aimed at hydration, brightening and ageing concerns, waxing and tinting, tanning, and professional makeup for special occasions, photoshoots and corporate events. Bridal makeup and gift vouchers are available, and the studio retails Medik8, iS Clinical, Vida Glow and ISSADA skincare. Appointments run Tuesday to Saturday.
highlights: Stocks Medik8, iS Clinical, Vida Glow and ISSADA
Open Tuesday to Saturday by appointment

name: Conspiracy Tattoo
description: Tattoo studio at 27 Baylis Street doing custom designs as well as pre-existing artwork. The studio describes medical grade hygiene using single-use needles and autoclave sterilisation, and is a member of the Australian Tattooists Guild.
highlights: Member of the Australian Tattooists Guild

name: Possums Early Learning Centre
description: Long day care centre at 7 Forsyth Street for children from six weeks to five years, running two rooms, Little Possums and the Preschool Room. The centre operates 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday, 52 weeks a year excluding public holidays, and families can access the Child Care Subsidy.
highlights: Long day care from six weeks to five years

name: CBM Meats
description: Wholesale and retail butcher located at the rear of 61 Baylis Street, Wagga Wagga. The shop sells premium cuts, smallgoods and smoked meats, with a range built around Riverina Angus beef, Australian pork and Riverina lamb. It trades weekdays 9am to 6pm and weekends 9am to 3pm.
highlights: Riverina Angus beef and Riverina lamb
Behind the Victoria Hotel on Baylis Street

name: Little Triffids Flowers
description: Florist and gift shop at 30 Fitzmaurice Street selling bouquets, potted plants and a gift range that takes in jewellery, baby items, beauty products, books, stationery, food and drink, garden wares and homewares. The shop does wedding and funeral flowers and runs workshops. Open Monday 9am to 2pm, Tuesday to Friday 9am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to 2pm.

name: Kidsons Cycles
description: Bike shop at 105 Fitzmaurice Street stocking road and mountain bikes from Merida, Cervelo, Specialized, Trek and Cannondale, BMX from DK, Fit Bike Co, GT and Kink, and kids bikes. The workshop offers repairs and a range of service packages from a deluxe bike wash to roadworthy, general, premium and platinum services, plus bike fitting sessions of about an hour. New bikes come with a free first service.
highlights: Road, mountain, BMX and kids bikes
Merida, Cervelo, Specialized, Trek and Cannondale
Free first service with a new bike

name: Gateway Bookshop
description: Independent bookshop in The Piazza on Baylis Street. The range covers children's and adult fiction, non-fiction, educational resources across several levels, special edition books and teacher diaries, and the shop also runs VR escape room experiences. Open Tuesday to Friday 10am to 5pm and Saturday 10am to 1pm.

name: Diamonds on Baylis Jewellers
description: Jewellery shop at 80 Baylis Street that has traded since 1984 and handcrafts rings, chains, pendants, earrings and bracelets in 9ct and 18ct yellow, white and rose gold. Stones used include diamonds, peridot, aquamarine, morganite, ruby and topaz, and the shop carries Adina and Citizen watches. On-site services cover custom design, repairs and restoration, ring resizing, stone resetting and appraisals.
highlights: On-site repairs, resizing and stone resetting

name: Allison Music Wagga
description: Locally owned music shop at 85 Forsyth Street that says it has served Wagga Wagga and the Riverina for over 23 years. Stock covers acoustic, electric, classical and bass guitars, amplifiers, acoustic and digital drums, acoustic and digital pianos, keyboards, folk instruments such as banjo, mandolin, ukulele and harmonica, orchestral instruments, PA and recording gear, sheet music and apparel.

name: Riverina Driving Academy
description: Driving school teaching learner drivers across Wagga Wagga and district, including Ashmont, Bourkelands, Estella, Forest Hill, Glenfield Park, Gumly Gumly, Kooringal, Lake Albert, Lloyd, Mount Austin, Tatton, Tolland and Turvey Park. Lessons run 60 minutes in dual-control automatic Honda Jazz cars, with a package of five lessons plus a sixth at half price. The instructor is Keys2Drive accredited.
highlights: Five lesson package with sixth at half price
Covers Wagga suburbs and nearby villages
Pick-up across Wagga Wagga and district

name: Rapley's Nursery and Landscape Supplies
description: Nursery and landscape supply yard at 56 Cummins Road, Lake Albert. The business sells locally grown plants and advanced trees alongside soils, mulches and landscape products, and offers planting advice, planning and design assistance, soil testing and delivery through Wagga Wagga and surrounding areas. Open weekdays 8am to 5pm and weekends 8:30am to 3pm.
highlights: Locally grown plants and advanced trees

name: Storehouse Botanica
description: Florist and gift store at 1 Humphrys Street, Junee. Arrangements are offered in pastel, tonal, bright and wildflower styles, and the shop also carries home fragrance, bath and body products, books, clothing and accessories. Next business day delivery is available in Junee and surrounding areas.
highlights: Home fragrance, bath and body gifts
Next business day delivery in Junee and district

name: Monty & Moo
description: Clothing, gifts and homewares store on Albury Street, Holbrook. The range covers dresses, shirts, knitwear and jackets, accessories including belts, jewellery, handbags and footwear, plus home and garden goods, bath and beauty products, greeting cards and stationery.

name: Skinner & Associates
description: Law firm founded in 1969 with an office at 24 Balfour Street, Culcairn and a second office in Albury. Practice areas listed are commercial and corporate law, conveyancing and property law, family law, wills and estates, dispute resolution and litigation, employment law, public notary work and court and tribunal appearances.
highlights: Family law and wills and estates

name: Custom Music
description: Music store on East Street, Narrandera, one of three Custom Music stores along with Griffith and Wagga Wagga. Stock includes guitars, ukuleles, amplifiers, drums, pianos, brass and wind instruments, violins and home recording equipment, and the business sells, installs and services PA systems and lighting for schools, clubs and churches. The Narrandera store opens weekdays 10am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to noon.
highlights: Guitars, drums, pianos and orchestral instruments
Installation and service for schools, clubs and churches
Stores at Narrandera, Griffith and Wagga Wagga

name: International Hotel Wagga Wagga
description: A hotel on the corner of the Sturt Highway and Lake Albert Road with 81 hotel rooms and suites, minutes from the Wagga Wagga CBD. Free Wi-Fi is provided and room service comes from Pinnacle's Restaurant and Bar, where the executive chef builds seasonal menus around regional produce. Apartment accommodation is also offered at the Mill Residence.
addressLine: Corner Sturt Highway and Lake Albert Road
highlights: Pinnacle's Restaurant and Bar on site
Wheelchair access and disability awareness trained staff

name: Mercure Wagga Wagga
description: A central Morgan Street hotel with 86 rooms made up of hotel rooms and self-contained serviced apartments, the apartments taking up to nine guests. Rooms have flat-screen TVs with free Foxtel, free Wi-Fi, in-room safes and tea and coffee facilities. There is a swimming pool, free on-site parking, four meeting rooms and the One Morgan Street restaurant and bar, plus free pool passes to the Oasis Aquatic Centre across the road.
highlights: One Morgan Street restaurant and bar
Four meeting rooms for events and weddings
Free pool passes to Oasis Aquatic Centre

name: Mantra Pavilion Hotel Wagga Wagga
description: A Kincaid Street hotel built around a 109-foot fabric roof, the largest of its kind in the world. Rooms include marble bathrooms, spas, mini-bars and balcony access. The hotel provides free Wi-Fi throughout, an arrival and departure lounge, tour desk, conference and meeting facilities, on-site parking and guest laundry, and sits alongside the city's restaurants, cafes, microbrewery and shopping.
highlights: Rooms with marble bathrooms and spas

name: Townhouse Hotel Wagga
description: A Morgan Street hotel in downtown Wagga Wagga with several room types and separate apartments. Guests get free use of the indoor heated aquatic centre and gym directly across the road, plus free wireless internet throughout. The Oakroom Restaurant and Bar serves guests in the restaurant or by room service.
highlights: Oakroom Restaurant and Bar on site
Free entry to the aquatic centre and gym across the road
Apartments as well as hotel rooms

name: St Hugh Hotel
description: A Forsyth Street hotel in central Wagga Wagga with four room categories: St Hugh Signature, Family, Accessible and Luxury. Rooms have custom king beds, smart TVs and secured Wi-Fi, and guest services run seven days a week. The hotel lists wheelchair access, accessible bathrooms and parking, hearing loop systems and staff trained in disability awareness.
highlights: Signature, Family, Accessible and Luxury rooms
Custom king beds and smart TVs

name: The Charles Boutique Hotel & Dining
description: A boutique hotel on Tarcutta Street with boutique king rooms, hotel rooms, suites and self-contained apartments finished in modern interiors. The Charles Dining Room serves dinner Tuesday to Saturday from 5:30pm and breakfast Tuesday to Friday from 6:45am, with tasting menus and a la carte built on Riverina ingredients. Vegan and gluten free options are catered for.
highlights: Boutique king rooms, suites and self-contained apartments
The Charles Dining Room open Tuesday to Saturday for dinner
Tasting menu and a la carte using Riverina produce

name: Quality Hotel Rules Club Wagga
description: A hotel of 79 units, four of them accessible, connected directly to the Rules Club precinct on Fernleigh Road. Rooms are soundproofed and air conditioned with 137cm smart TVs, free Wi-Fi or Ethernet and complimentary tea, coffee and biscuits. There is secure card-access parking, an electric vehicle charging station, conference and board rooms, fitness centre access and pushbikes for guests, with the club's cafe, restaurant and sports bar next door.
highlights: Directly connected to the Rules Club
Guest pushbikes and fitness centre access

name: Wagga RSL Motel & Apartments
description: Motel accommodation within the Wagga RSL Club on Kincaid Street. Room types run from Executive Suite and Easy Access Suite through Executive, Deluxe, Corner and Luxury Spa Suites, plus four self-contained two-bedroom apartments sleeping up to five. There is a solar heated pool, and guests have direct access to the club's dining venues, bars and live entertainment. The city centre is about a ten minute walk.
highlights: Executive, Deluxe, Corner and Luxury Spa Suites
Club dining, bars and entertainment on site
About ten minutes walk to the city centre

name: Boulevarde Motor Inn
description: An Edward Street motor inn where all rooms are ground floor, air conditioned and fully furnished, with 55 inch 4K Samsung TVs carrying Foxtel and free Netflix. The property has gardens, a barbecue area, an outdoor swimming pool and a guest laundry, and family rooms are available. It sits near the CBD and both the Wagga Wagga Rural Referral and Calvary hospitals.
highlights: All rooms on the ground floor
Foxtel and free Netflix in rooms

name: Best Western Ambassador Motor Inn & Apartments
description: A motor inn on Edward Street with Queen Rooms, Deluxe Twin, Accessible Twin, Family Suite, Signature Spa Suite and Two Bedroom Villa accommodation. Rooms carry 43 inch smart TVs, free wireless internet, electric blankets and work desks, with a kitchenette or full kitchen depending on the type. The property has an outdoor saltwater pool open October to April, a barbecue and garden area, free on-site parking and a self-service guest laundry, with continental breakfast seven days.
highlights: Rooms, family suites, spa suite and two bedroom villas
Outdoor saltwater pool October to April

name: Club Motel and Apartments
description: A Morgan Street motel with accommodation ranging from economy single rooms to larger deluxe rooms with small kitchens and two-bedroom family units. Free secure parking, Wi-Fi and 24 hour service are provided and late check-ins are accepted. There is a steakhouse and bar on site, with a pool and gym across the road and the main street shops and restaurants nearby.
highlights: Economy singles through to two-bedroom family units
Pool and gym across the road

name: Seven Inn
description: A 26-room motor inn on the Sturt Highway at Gumly Gumly, just east of Wagga Wagga. Rooms have reverse cycle air conditioning, a 40 inch smart television, work desk, open wardrobe, blackout curtains, fridge, microwave and tea and coffee facilities. The grounds include a saltwater outdoor pool, barbecue facilities, gardens and outdoor seating. Wagga Airport and the RAAF base are about seven minutes away, and Lake Albert and the Botanic Gardens about eight.
highlights: Fridge and microwave in every room
About seven minutes to Wagga Airport and the RAAF base

name: BIG4 Ingenia Holidays Wagga Wagga
description: A riverside holiday park on Hammond Avenue about 2km from the Wagga Wagga town centre, backing onto the Murrumbidgee River. Accommodation covers cabins for different group sizes and budgets plus caravan and camping sites. Facilities include a swimming pool, adventure playground, camp kitchen, walking tracks, river access with a private boat launch, EV charging and a 24 hour service station. Some sites and cabins are pet friendly.
highlights: Cabins plus caravan and camping sites
Murrumbidgee River access and private boat launch

name: Horseshoe Tourist Park
description: A caravan park in a lagoon setting about seven minutes north of the Wagga Wagga CBD. Sites include drive-thru powered sites, ensuite powered sites and big rig sites, with two-bedroom standard cabins, deluxe studios and deluxe villas for cabin stays. Facilities cover an outdoor swimming pool, free barbecues, free Wi-Fi and a function room with an outdoor barbecue area. All sites are gravel and not suited to tents, swags or soft floor campers, and pets are not permitted. Charles Sturt University is about four minutes away.
highlights: Drive-thru, ensuite and big rig powered sites
Standard cabins, deluxe studios and deluxe villas
Function room with outdoor barbecue area
Four minutes from Charles Sturt University

name: Globe Apartments
description: Refurbished self-contained serviced apartments on the corner of Peter and Morgan Streets, one block from the main street. The building was the Globe Hotel in the 1880s. Apartments sleep up to six people, and the property has barbecue facilities and secure parking and takes both short and extended stays.
highlights: Self-contained apartments sleeping up to six
Housed in the 1880s Globe Hotel building

name: Civic Apartments
description: Self-contained apartments on Baylis Street running from a Queen Studio Suite with kitchenette through open plan, one-bedroom, two-bedroom and two-bedroom accessible suites with full kitchens. Check-in is self-directed using secure access codes and there is a gated, coded-access car park. Each stay includes Wi-Fi, streaming-capable televisions, tea, coffee, hot chocolate and local bottled water, and porta cots, highchairs, prams and a shared guest laundry are available.
highlights: Studio through to two-bedroom accessible suites
Porta cots, highchairs and prams available
Walking distance to the Riverwalk and galleries

name: The Riverine Club
description: Wagga's private club, offering 13 guest rooms on the first floor for members, reciprocal members and their guests. Some rooms have balconies looking over the Murrumbidgee River. There are two large shared bathrooms, a sitting room and a breakfast area, with continental breakfast available on request and discounted rates for large groups and extended stays. Guests also get access to member facilities including the private members bar and billiards room.
highlights: 13 guest rooms in the Wagga CBD
Members bar, billiards room and squash court
Discounts for groups and extended stays

name: Brae View Villas 1 and 2
description: Two self-contained two-bedroom villas in a quiet residential part of Kooringal, each sleeping five. Both have fully equipped kitchens, large dining areas, lounges with televisions, central heating and cooling and lock-up garages. Lake Albert and its walking and cycling tracks are close by, as is the Kooringal Shopping Centre.
highlights: Fully equipped kitchens and lock-up garages
Near Lake Albert and Kooringal Shopping Centre

name: Rosewood Cottage
description: A holiday cottage in the leafy residential suburb of Turvey Park. It is a double brick post-war classic built by a local family in the forties, kept with its period detail and fitted out with restored vintage furnishings. It suits families and guests after a quiet location and retro character.
highlights: Double brick post-war cottage from the 1940s
Period detail and restored vintage furnishings

name: The Old Billiard Shop
description: A renovated corner shop in Turvey Park that was once a billiard store, now let as accommodation. The stay is one large room with brass sash windows and original floorboards, with blackout blinds on the oversized windows for privacy. The bathroom is reached through an enclosed outdoor area a few steps from the room, and all fixtures are newly installed.
highlights: Brass sash windows and original floorboards
Blackout blinds on the oversized windows
Bathroom via an enclosed outdoor area

name: Nice on Nilma
description: A self-contained Wagga Wagga cottage let through Henderson's Houses and aimed at groups who want their own beds rather than shared sleeping. It has seven separate beds, one double and six singles, across three bedrooms, plus a fully enclosed sun room. Split system air conditioning runs in the lounge and bedrooms.
highlights: Seven separate beds across three bedrooms
Suited to families and larger groups

name: The Leagues
description: A modern heritage-style three-storey home on Gurwood Street purpose built for overnight and short-term stays. Rooms take one to four people each and all have heating and cooling, with continental breakfast included. It is close to the Wagga Wagga CBD, the hospital, the RSL and the Murrumbidgee Turf Club, and within driving distance of Kapooka Army Base and the Forest Hill RAAF base.
highlights: Rooms for one to four people
Heating and cooling in all rooms
Near the CBD, hospital and Turf Club

name: Junee Tourist Park
description: A caravan and camping park within walking distance of the Junee Licorice and Chocolate Factory. It has two-bedroom self-contained cabins in budget and deluxe versions, plus powered, non-powered, tent and fifth wheeler sites and drive-through sites for caravans and motorhomes. Facilities include a camp kitchen, laundry and modern amenities. The park is pet friendly, has a dog agility park alongside it and looks out over Park Dam.
highlights: Budget and deluxe two-bedroom self-contained cabins
Large powered, non-powered and drive-through sites
Pet friendly with a dog agility park alongside
Walking distance to the Licorice and Chocolate Factory

name: The Crossing Motel
description: A Junee motel on Seignior Street with air conditioned rooms, free Wi-Fi and smart TVs. The Roundhouse Restaurant serves seasonal a la carte meals using locally sourced produce and puts together luncheon hampers, with the restaurant and bar running 7am to 9pm. There is a guests-only saltwater outdoor pool, free guest laundry and on-site parking with room for large vehicles, coach groups, car clubs and motorcycle groups.
highlights: Roundhouse Restaurant and bar on site
Parking for large vehicles and coach groups

name: Fig Tree Motel
description: A budget motel on Cadell Street about 150m from the Narrandera town centre. Room types run from budget units through to two-bedroom family suites that take up to seven guests. It is set up for both business travellers and people driving the Newell Highway, with shops, restaurants and sporting facilities close by.
highlights: Budget units through to two-bedroom family suites
Family suites sleeping up to seven

name: Lake Talbot Tourist Park
description: A caravan, camping and cabin park on Gordon Street set on the shores of Lake Talbot at Narrandera. Bookings can be made through the park's own online system. Accessible features listed include accessible parking, accessible bathroom fixtures, grab rails and slip-resistant pathways.
highlights: On the shores of Lake Talbot
Accessible parking, grab rails and slip-resistant paths

name: Historic Star Lodge and Station Masters House
description: National Trust and heritage listed lodgings built beside the restored Narrandera Railway Station, in the town's early heritage district. Rooms are spacious and furnished with quality Australian and Anglo-European antiques in keeping with the buildings. The lodge featured on the Australian passport in 2009.
highlights: Purpose built beside the restored railway station
Featured on the Australian passport in 2009

name: The Leeton Heritage Motor Inn
description: A Yanco Avenue motor inn with 33 spacious ground-floor rooms, all air conditioned and with WiFi, including two accessible rooms. There is an outdoor saltwater swimming pool, guest barbecue facilities, a picnic area, laundry and EV charging. Charley's is the licensed on-site restaurant and event space, cooked and continental breakfast is served seven days and in-room dining runs Monday to Thursday. Leeton's CBD, golf course, sporting complex and RSL club are nearby.
highlights: 33 ground-floor rooms including two accessible rooms
Charley's licensed restaurant and event space
Cooked and continental breakfast seven days

name: Goldtera Motor Inn
description: A 12-room motor inn in the Temora CBD, directly opposite the Temora Ex-Services Memorial Club which runs it. Rooms have queen beds, mini bars, reverse-cycle air conditioning, LCD televisions with DVD players, free WiFi, cutlery and crockery, and an iron and ironing board. There is a swimming pool and barbecue area, and one twin room is fully wheelchair accessible. The Aviation Museum, Rural Museum and Lake Centenary are a short drive away.
highlights: Directly opposite the Temora Ex-Services Memorial Club
Walking distance to shops and restaurants

name: Kimo Estate
description: A 7,000 acre working farm on Nangus Road about ten minutes from Gundagai. Accommodation covers three off-grid EcoHuts set on a hilltop above the Murrumbidgee River flats, each with a private hot tub, a set of renovated 100-year-old workers' cottages suited to families, and Shearers Quarters with six bedrooms for larger groups.
highlights: Three off-grid EcoHuts with private hot tubs

name: Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens
description: The Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens sit at the base of Willans Hill and cover 22 acres. Within the grounds are a mini zoo, a free flight aviary, a children's adventure playground and a rainforest section, plus the Tree Chapel and a Chinese Pavilion. Garden areas showcase camellias, cacti and succulents, proteas, Australian natives and roses. Covered barbecues are available and the Willans Hill Miniature Railway runs through the gardens on the first and third Sunday of each month.
highlights: Mini zoo and free flight aviary
Camellia, cactus, protea, native and rose gardens

name: Museum of the Riverina - Botanic Gardens Site
description: The Botanic Gardens site is one of the Museum of the Riverina's two venues, sitting beside the Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens. It runs changing exhibitions along with workshops, events and school programs, and includes a historic schoolhouse in its grounds. General admission is free and all public spaces are wheelchair accessible by lift and pathway.
highlights: Accessible parking bay near the entrance
Free tea, coffee and water in the Community Education Space

name: Museum of the Riverina - Historic Council Chambers
description: The Historic Council Chambers on Baylis Street is the Museum of the Riverina's city-centre site. The museum is a social history museum combining touring shows of national significance with local stories, and across its two sites it cares for more than 15,000 objects, photographs, textiles and paper-based materials.
highlights: City-centre site in the historic council chambers

name: Wagga Wagga Art Gallery
description: Wagga Wagga Art Gallery shows work by Riverina artists alongside touring exhibitions from around Australia, with about forty exhibitions and displays each year. Its showpiece is the National Art Glass Gallery, home to Australia's largest and most significant collection of contemporary art glass, holding roughly 400 pieces.
addressLine: Morrow Street, Civic Centre corner Baylis Street
highlights: National Art Glass Gallery and the National Art Glass Collection
Around 40 exhibitions and displays a year
Wheelchair accessible with support for vision and hearing loss

name: Willans Hill Miniature Railway
description: The Willans Hill Miniature Railway runs inside the Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens, with an authentic station and booking office. The track weaves through a garden setting, woodlands, a tunnel and over a bridge. Trains run on the first and third Sunday of each month, and covered footwear is essential to ride. An invitation run each November brings model train enthusiasts from around Australia.
highlights: Runs the first and third Sunday of each month
Track through woodlands, a tunnel and over a bridge

name: Wagga Wagga Rail Heritage Station Museum
description: Set on the platform of the historic Wagga Wagga Railway Station, this museum displays photographs and railway memorabilia covering the local history of the railway. Across the railway pedestrian bridge are the Rail Heritage Gang Sheds, holding railway trikes, tools and photographs in two sheds once used by track maintenance gangs, and a model trains display with several working HO and N scale layouts. The three locations keep different opening times.
highlights: On the historic Wagga Wagga Railway Station platform
Gang Sheds display of railway trikes and tools
Working HO and N scale model railway layouts

name: Wagga Steam and Vintage Engine Museum
description: Operated by the Wagga Historic Engine Club Inc, this museum displays working engines including shearing machines and all types of stationary engines, along with vintage steam and oil engines. It opens on the first and third Sunday of the month, or by appointment, for a gold coin donation.
addressLine: Lord Baden Powell Drive, Willans Hill
highlights: Run by the Wagga Historic Engine Club Inc
Working steam, oil and stationary engines
Open first and third Sunday of the month, or by appointment

name: RAAF Wagga Aviation Heritage Centre
description: The RAAF Wagga Aviation Heritage Centre covers Air Force history and the RAAF's involvement in the Riverina. Static display aircraft beside the centre represent more than 50 years of RAAF flying history and can be viewed and photographed up close. Inside, heritage artefacts are set out in themed rooms including a Community Room with a rotating display on military history and the contribution of people from Wagga Wagga and the Riverina.
highlights: Static display aircraft spanning over 50 years of RAAF flying
Themed display rooms of Air Force artefacts
Community Room with rotating regional displays
Last remaining Riverina World War II base of its network

name: Lake Albert
description: Lake Albert is one of Wagga's most used recreational areas, catering for boating, fishing, swimming and other aquatic activities. A five-and-a-half kilometre circuit walking track rings the lake and is popular with walkers, joggers and bike riders, with eight fitness stations set over 800 metres on the eastern side. Boat ramps are at Bosley Park next to the Wagga Wagga Boat Club and at Apex Park, which also has a children's playground with a separate fenced area for smaller children.
highlights: 5.5 km circuit walking and cycling track
Eight outdoor fitness stations on the eastern side
Boat ramps at Bosley Park and Apex Park
Playground with fenced area for small children

name: Riverside Wagga Beach
description: Riverside Wagga Beach is a sandy river beach on the Murrumbidgee about five minutes from the CBD, with grassed shady picnic areas, sheltered barbecues, sculptures and event spaces. Swimmers cool off in the river during the warmer months and paddlers launch kayaks and canoes from here. It also has a large destination playground catering for all ages and abilities, food and drink vans nearby, and forms part of the Wiradjuri Walking Track.
highlights: Sandy beach on the Murrumbidgee River
Large destination playground for all ages and abilities

name: Oasis Aquatic Centre
description: The Oasis Aquatic Centre in the middle of Wagga runs year round. Indoors there is a 25-metre pool, leisure pools including the Turbo Pool and mushrooms, toddler pools and a program pool used for swimming lessons and hydrotherapy. Outdoors there is a 50-metre pool and a diving pool with one-metre and three-metre springboards and a five-metre platform. The centre has free barbecues, a children's playground and accessible change rooms, and is used by water polo, diving and triathlon groups.
highlights: Indoor 25 m pool and outdoor 50 m pool
Diving pool with springboards and a 5 m platform
Turbo Pool, mushrooms and toddler pools
Learn to Swim classes for adults and children
Free barbecues and a children's playground

name: Wiradjuri Trail
description: The Wiradjuri Trail is a walking and cycling route of about 42 kilometres that circles much of Wagga Wagga, taking in riverbanks and hilltops. It winds through the Birramal Conservation Area, Silvalite Reserve and Pomingalarna Reserve. The Wollundry Loop, a 12.1 kilometre section, follows part of the Murrumbidgee River and the perimeter of the Wollundry Lagoon, and a popular return route starts at the Visitor Information Centre and takes in Wagga Beach, the Cadell Place laneway murals, Wiradjuri Reserve and Marrambidya Wetland.
highlights: About 42 km of walking and cycling trail
Passes Birramal, Silvalite and Pomingalarna reserves
Links Wagga Beach, Cadell Place murals and Marrambidya Wetland

name: Marrambidya Wetland
description: Marrambidya Wetland is a 20-hectare reserve beside the Murrumbidgee River a few minutes from the city centre. It has two kilometres of connected Grade 2 walking tracks, bird hides for watching waterbirds and an elevated viewing platform over the whole wetland. There is a cultural demonstration area with a Wiradjuri campsite, gunyahs and a bora ring, a Wiradjuri Healing Place, and an outdoor art gallery of works at the car park entry. Dogs on leads are welcome.
highlights: Two kilometres of Grade 2 walking tracks
Bird hides and an elevated viewing platform
Wiradjuri cultural demonstration area and Healing Place
Outdoor art gallery at the entry

name: Pomingalarna Reserve
description: Pomingalarna Reserve sits on part of the Wiradjuri Trail about ten minutes from the Wagga Wagga CBD and is used by bushwalkers, runners and riders. A marked 13-kilometre bushland mountain bike trail runs through native bushland where kangaroos, wallabies, lizards and birds are common. The reserve is also home to Wagga Wagga's Multisport Cycling Complex, with a criterium track, BMX track, jump tracks, pump tracks, a cycling education area, a velodrome and a mountain bike playground loop. The climb to the top gives some of the best views back over the city.
highlights: 13 km marked bushland mountain bike trail
Multisport Cycling Complex with criterium and BMX tracks
Velodrome, pump tracks and jump tracks
Cycling education area and mountain bike playground loop
Lookout over Wagga Wagga from the summit

name: Birramal Conservation Area
description: Birramal Conservation Area is a 128-hectare site set aside for environmental conservation, taking in the section of the Wiradjuri Trail between the Olympic Highway and Holbrook Road. It can be explored on foot or by bike and offers views over Wagga Wagga and surrounds. The site protects an endangered White Box Woodland community that supports the locally endangered squirrel glider, and glider poles, new tree plantings and artificial nest boxes are visible along the way.
highlights: 128-hectare conservation area on the Wiradjuri Trail
Squirrel glider habitat with glider poles and nest boxes
Walking and mountain biking with views over the city

name: Victory Memorial Gardens
description: The Victory Memorial Gardens were established in 1925 as a tribute to those who fought and died in the First World War, and were designed by Thomas Kerr, designer of the Sydney Botanic Gardens. They run along the banks of the Wollundry Lagoon in the heart of Wagga Wagga. Visitors commonly feed the ducks and water birds, and the geese cross Ivan Jack Drive with right of way. The land was formerly the site of the Old Police Barracks and its police paddocks.
highlights: Established 1925 as a First World War memorial
On the banks of Wollundry Lagoon in the CBD

name: Forum 6 Cinemas Wagga Wagga
description: Forum 6 is a six-cinema complex in the heart of Wagga Wagga. The programme runs from big blockbusters through to art house features, and also includes classic silver screen movies, operas from the MET, special events and midnight premieres. Session times, trading hours and pricing are published on the cinema's website and Facebook page.
highlights: Six screens in the Wagga CBD
Blockbusters, art house and classic films
MET opera screenings and special events
Wheelchair accessible with vision and hearing support

name: Wagga Bowl
description: Wagga Bowl is a ten pin bowling and entertainment centre on Trail Street, trading seven days. It runs birthday and party packages, sells gift vouchers and has a large media screen over the lanes. A movie and bowl deal runs during the school holidays. Bookings are recommended on Saturdays, Sundays and during school and public holidays.
highlights: Ten pin bowling seven days a week
Movie and bowl deal in school holidays
Bookings recommended on weekends and holidays

name: Vortex Entertainment
description: Vortex Entertainment is an indoor entertainment centre in the Wagga CBD. Attractions include six-metre rock climbing walls, a high ropes course, a ninja course, dedicated toddler play areas, bumper cars, virtual reality experiences and 18 holes of mini golf. It also has private party rooms and a cafe serving hot and cold food and drinks, and runs quiet sessions.
highlights: Toddler play areas and private party rooms

name: Noah's Ark Indoor Play Centre
description: Noah's Ark is an indoor play and party centre on Hammond Avenue for children under 12, air-conditioned year round. Equipment includes slides, ball pools, flying foxes, crawl tunnels, squeeze rollers and a cosy coupe car track, and plaster painting is also available. The cafe serves hot and cold food along with kids' meals. Socks are required.
highlights: Play and party centre for children under 12
Slides, ball pools, flying foxes and crawl tunnels
Cosy coupe car track and plaster painting

name: Wagga Wagga Sailing Club
description: The Wagga Wagga Sailing Club races on Lake Albert and has around 40 members, with twenty to twenty-five sailors racing regularly. Racing is each Saturday through the season, with briefing at 2pm and the start at 2.30pm. Visitors are welcome to bring their own boat or use a club boat, and crew positions are available. The club runs learn to sail courses through the warmer months and has a radio-controlled sailing section.
highlights: Saturday racing on Lake Albert, briefing 2pm
Learn to sail courses in the warmer months

name: Wagga City Aero Club
description: The Wagga City Aero Club has its clubhouse in the General Aviation Precinct on Elizabeth Avenue at Wagga Wagga Airport. Members include pilots of all ages and experience, aircraft owners and non-pilots, drawn from general aviation, airlines, commercial and recreational flying and the military. Social evenings run every Friday from 5.30pm, and a barbecue with flying competitions is held on the first Sunday of each month from noon. The club also runs a Young Eagles program for young people.
addressLine: General Aviation Precinct, Elizabeth Avenue, Wagga Wagga Airport
highlights: Clubhouse at Wagga Wagga Airport's general aviation precinct
Barbecue and flying competitions first Sunday of the month
Young Eagles program for young people

name: Men's Shed Wagga Wagga
description: Men's Shed Wagga Wagga Inc operates from Best Reserve on the corner of Veale Street and Ashmont Avenue. The shed runs a garage sale from Monday to Thursday between 8.15am and 11.45am, with items for sale changing regularly. The phone is answered between 8am and noon on weekdays.
addressLine: Best Reserve, corner of Veale Street and Ashmont Avenue
highlights: Based at Best Reserve, Veale Street and Ashmont Avenue
Garage sale Monday to Thursday, 8.15am to 11.45am

name: Wagga Wagga & District Family History Society
description: The Wagga Wagga & District Family History Society runs a library and research rooms at 24 Tarakan Avenue, Ashmont, open to the public and staffed by volunteers. Its collections include the Pastoral Review journals from 1891 to 1977, which contain photographs of First World War servicemen and nurses contributed by families. The society publishes research CDs, including a Wagga Wagga and district births, deaths, marriages and in memoriams index with more than 49,500 entries.
highlights: Public research rooms and library at Ashmont
Wagga Wagga and district BDM index on CD
Volunteer staffed, phone ahead to confirm opening
Extended hours to 4pm Mondays and Wednesdays during daylight saving

name: Wagga Wagga & District Historical Society
description: The Wagga Wagga & District Historical Society researches and publishes local history and takes enquiries through its website and Facebook page. It does not keep a public room; its historical material is held by Charles Sturt University Regional Archives, the Museum of the Riverina and the Wagga Wagga City Library local history collection. The society was one of the local partners that funded the digitisation of the Wagga Wagga Rate and Valuation books now available through NSW State Archives, and it publishes the Bidgee Whaler articles written by Sylvia Walsh.
highlights: Collections held at CSU Regional Archives, Museum of the Riverina and the city library
Partner in digitising the Wagga Wagga Rate and Valuation books
Enquiries by email and through the website

name: Wagga Cycling Club
description: Wagga Cycling Club is a family orientated club focused on track, criterium and road racing. Its coaches run rider development programs for all ages at training nights across the summer and winter seasons. The club holds road racing events in winter and the Golden Wheel two day track carnival in summer.
highlights: Coached rider development programs for all ages
Training nights in summer and winter seasons
Golden Wheel two day track carnival in summer

name: Wagga Wagga Combined Hockey Association
description: Wagga Hockey runs the local hockey competitions at the Jubilee Park Hockey Complex on artificial playing surfaces. Junior competitions are mixed and start at Under 9, Under 11, Under 13 and Under 16, all played on Friday nights. There are three divisions each of men's and women's competition, with senior matches on Saturday afternoons from 11am and lights on both fields allowing play into the evening. The association was formed after the 2005 season when the separate men's and women's associations merged.
highlights: Games at the Jubilee Park Hockey Complex
Mixed junior competitions from Under 9 to Under 16 on Friday nights
Three divisions each of men's and women's competition
Formed in 2005 from the men's and women's associations

name: Football Wagga
description: Football Wagga is the association that runs organised football in Wagga Wagga, covering MiniRoos, junior and senior competitions along with a Football4All AllStars competition and a skill acquisition development program. It publishes fixtures and results, manages referees and coordinates ground availability and closures, with Rawlings Park as the main venue.
highlights: Fixtures, results and ground closures published online

name: Wagga Wagga Bridge Club
description: The Wagga Wagga Bridge Club plays at 7 Bolton Street and runs sessions each week spread between daytime and evening time slots. It offers free beginner classes and welcomes visitors and new members. The club is affiliated with the Australian Bridge Federation and awards ABF masterpoints, and it hosts congresses that draw players from other clubs.
highlights: Affiliated with the Australian Bridge Federation
Hosts the annual Wagga Wagga Congress

name: Wagga City Golf Club
description: Wagga City Golf Club is about five minutes west of the Wagga Wagga CBD off the Sturt Highway at 5 McNickle Road, Moorong. The course is open every day except Christmas Day from 6am to 6pm, and there is no requirement to be a member to play, with social golfers welcome. The club has a pro shop, offers lessons and vouchers, and hosts corporate golf days and functions. Light refreshments including sandwiches, pies and sausages are available, along with soft drinks and mid strength beers. There is no driving range.
highlights: Open every day except Christmas Day, 6am to 6pm
Five minutes west of the CBD off the Sturt Highway

name: Wagga Wagga School of Arts Community Theatre
description: SoACT, the Wagga Wagga School of Arts Community Theatre, is a community theatre company that stages a season of plays and musicals each year and posts audition notices for each production. Recent seasons have included The Sound of Music, The Pirates of Penzance, And Then There Were None, A Broadcast Coup and The Female of the Species, along with the Riverina Water Ten x 10 Playfest of short plays. The company sells memberships and show gift vouchers.
highlights: Community theatre company staging a full season each year
Riverina Water Ten x 10 Playfest of short plays
Open audition notices for each production
Archive of past production videos for members

name: Wagga Wagga Swim Club
description: Established in 1897, the Wagga Wagga Swim Club is one of the oldest swimming clubs in New South Wales. It runs five squads from Development through to National, plus a Masters and recreational squad, and is led by head coach Gennadiy Labara with a committee and technical officials. The club holds club nights and club championships, enters carnivals and representative meets, and welcomes visiting swimmers.
highlights: Five squads from Development to National level

name: Murrumbidgee Landcare
description: Murrumbidgee Landcare Inc is a natural resource management organisation with its office in the Tulloch Business Offices at 66 Coleman Street, Turvey Park. Its staff include a chief executive officer, a manager of projects and partnerships, a regional Landcare coordinator and a regional Aboriginal Landcare coordinator, working from the Wagga Wagga office through the week. It runs projects, events and resources for Landcare groups across the Murrumbidgee.
highlights: Wagga Wagga office in the Tulloch Business Offices
Regional Landcare coordination across the Murrumbidgee
Projects, events and resources for member groups

name: ErinEarth
description: ErinEarth is a sustainable living education centre and volunteering community on Kildare Street in Turvey Park. The garden demonstrates organic vegetable growing and a water-efficient native plant garden, and is set up as a quiet space for nature connection, reflection and nature play. It hosts regular community open days, education sessions and a weekly garden volunteering program on Thursday mornings.
highlights: Weekly volunteering program on Thursday mornings

name: Wagga Basketball
description: Wagga Basketball, home of the Heat, runs junior and senior competitions for around 1000 members at PCYC Wagga Wagga. It fields representative teams in junior and senior leagues from Under 12s through to open divisions in the Waratah State League and other competitions. Programs include Aussie Hoops, an academy program and Blazing Hoops, a free girls program, and the association is run by a volunteer board.
highlights: Junior and senior competitions at PCYC Wagga Wagga
Representative teams from Under 12s to open age
Aussie Hoops, academy and free Blazing Hoops girls programs

name: Temora Aviation Museum
description: The Temora Aviation Museum is built on the site of the former No. 10 Elementary Flying Training School, established by the RAAF in May 1941, and holds a flying collection of Australian ex-military aircraft. Visitors can take a guided tour with a volunteer or explore at their own pace with audio-visual presentations, watch a film in the 38-seat surround sound theatre, and see engineers at work from the viewing platform. There are landscaped gardens, picnic areas, an aviation themed playground, flight simulators and a cafe, and Aircraft Showcase flying days are held through the year.
highlights: Flying collection of Australian ex-military aircraft
Guided tours by volunteers and an audio tour
Aircraft Showcase flying days and flight simulators

name: Lake Centenary
description: Lake Centenary is four kilometres north of Temora and is used for power boating, water skiing, sailing, canoeing, swimming and fishing. A path circumnavigates the lake for walkers. The precinct also has a playground, self-weighted gym equipment, landscaped picnic areas and free barbecue facilities.
highlights: Power boating, water skiing and canoeing
Free barbecues and landscaped picnic areas

name: Junee Licorice & Chocolate Factory
description: The Junee Licorice & Chocolate Factory makes organic licorice and chocolate in a historic Junee flour mill and sells it across Australia and overseas. Visitors can take a guided tour of the factory, eat at The Mill Room Cafe and shop the retail range, and the site runs an events program through the year. It opens seven days a week from 9am to 4pm, every day except Anzac Day.
highlights: Organic licorice and chocolate made on site
Housed in a historic Junee flour mill
Open seven days, 9am to 4pm, except Anzac Day

name: Junee Roundhouse Railway Museum
description: The Junee Roundhouse is one of the few surviving working railway roundhouses in the Southern Hemisphere, unique in Australia for its size, fully circular form and 100 foot turntable. Opened in 1947 as the last steam locomotive depot built for New South Wales Railways, half the building is now a museum while the other half still services locomotives. Exhibits include steam and diesel locomotives, passenger carriages, a sleeping car, a rail motor, a mail van, the only workable steam driven accident crane in New South Wales and a large working model railway. Guided tour information is available at the admissions desk and self-guided tours are welcome.
highlights: Working railway roundhouse with a 100 foot turntable
Steam and diesel locomotives and heritage carriages
The only workable steam driven accident crane in NSW
Guided and self-guided tours, last admission 3.30pm

name: Junee Golf Club
description: Junee Golf Club plays an 18 hole, par 72 course. There are no bunkers but a couple of holes have out of bounds and other hazards, so club selection and accuracy matter. The course suits both average and longer hitters and is used for social rounds and competition. The clubhouse is managed by volunteers, has a bar and barbecue, and the club hosts regular events and private functions. Campsites are available at the grounds.
highlights: No bunkers but several out of bounds holes
Volunteer managed clubhouse with a bar
Barbecue and camping sites on site

name: Dog on the Tuckerbox
description: The Dog on the Tuckerbox pioneer monument stands five miles, or eight kilometres, north of Gundagai just off the Hume Highway. The statue was unveiled on 28 November 1932, honouring the bullock drivers who opened up the country and the dogs that travelled with them, a legend carried further by Jack O'Hagan's song. The precinct today has maintained gardens, Australian animal figurines, picnic areas and parking for cars, caravans and coaches, plus a kiosk and farm shop selling food, coffee, local produce and gifts. The Dog's Birthday is celebrated each November.
highlights: Eight kilometres north of Gundagai off the Hume Highway
Kiosk and farm shop open seven days
Gardens, animal figurines and picnic areas
Parking for cars, caravans and coaches

name: Lake Talbot Water Park
description: Lake Talbot Water Park at Narrandera has pools and three water slides, including an enclosed high-speed racer slide, plus a splash-and-play park. The lawned pool surrounds have shady picnic spots, barbecues and pool-level change rooms, and there is wheelchair access into the pools. A Skywalk off the car park gives views over Lake Talbot itself.
highlights: Three water slides including an enclosed racer slide
Lawned surrounds with barbecues and picnic spots
Skywalk with views over Lake Talbot

name: Tilyard Plumbing
description: Tilyard Plumbing is a locally owned plumbing business servicing Wagga Wagga and the wider Riverina, with more than 20 years in the trade and a stated focus on drainage and sewer work. Listed services include blocked drains, CCTV drain inspections, sewer renewals, stormwater, water service renewals, hot water systems, gas plumbing, maintenance, renovations and small to medium projects. Pre-purchase plumbing inspections and emergency after-hours plumbing are also offered. Service areas named on the site include Wagga Wagga, Boorooma, Gobbagombalin and North Wagga.
highlights: Blocked drains, sewer renewals and stormwater specialists
Licensed gas fitting, installations and safety checks

name: Aherns Plumbing Service
description: Aherns Plumbing Service has operated in Wagga Wagga and the surrounding region since 1994. 24/7 emergency plumbing, roofing and gas fitting

Gas fitting for LPG and natural gas
Blocked drains, drainage cleaning and sewage repairs

The business runs its own excavation equipment and offers after-hours work on request.

The business is licensed under NSW Fair Trading and offers free, no-obligation quotes.

highlights: Residential, commercial and industrial electrical work

Underground and data and fibre cabling

highlights: Servicing Wagga Wagga and the Riverina

Solar batteries and off-grid style storage

highlights: Solar panel and battery storage installation
Locally owned and operated in Wagga Wagga
Free quote requests through the site

First home buyer and finance information is also provided.

highlights: Three bedroom, four plus bedroom and acreage designs
House and land packages in Wagga suburbs
Fully inclusive quotes with no hidden extras

highlights: HIA member and CM3 safety prequalified

The site states more than 27 years of industry experience and award-winning heritage restoration work.
highlights: More than 27 years of industry experience

name: Sheathers Painting & Decorating
description: Sheathers Painting & Decorating is a Wagga Wagga painting business run by Tim and a team of about 20 painters, with a combined 60 years of experience. The team takes on repaints, commercial property work and pool painting, and hires local tradesmen and apprentices. Free quotes are offered.
highlights: Repaints, commercial property and pool painting

description: Shields Painting & Decorating carries out interior and exterior painting for homes and businesses in Wagga Wagga. The business offers a free site inspection and quote and fixed price contracts, and also services Temora, Tumut, Gundagai and Narrandera.

Trading hours are listed as open 24 hours, seven days.
highlights: Rebedding and pointing of ridge capping
Fascia and gutter repair and installation

highlights: Whole house or section guttering replacement
Residential plumbing and hot water systems

highlights: Nearly a decade of industry experience

highlights: Commercial, industrial, civil and residential contracts

Services Wagga Wagga and surrounding towns

highlights: Fabricates and installs domestic windows and doors
Shower screens, pool fences and balustrades

name: SG Glass & Aluminium
description: SG Glass & Aluminium is a Wagga Wagga glazier with more than 20 years of industry experience, cutting glass to size for residential and commercial properties. After-hours glass repairs are offered and trading hours are listed as 7am to 5pm every day with a 24 hour emergency service.
highlights: Glass cut to size for homes and businesses

Gas log fires, wood fires and portable heaters

highlights: Licensed in NSW, ACT and Victoria

highlights: Stock water systems, trenching and pipe laying

description: Wagga Directional Drilling is an industrial dry excavation business with over 20 years of drilling experience, serving domestic and commercial clients in Wagga Wagga and surrounding areas. highlights: Hydro vac excavation and waste disposal facility
Trenching, cable hauling and zero tension plough

name: Harrisons Joinery
description: Harrisons Joinery has delivered custom joinery across the Riverina for more than 40 years, working with clients on individually designed cabinetry rather than off-the-shelf solutions. highlights: More than 40 years in the Riverina
Licensed builder offering full home renovations

highlights: Also services Temora, Tumut, Gundagai, Albury and Cootamundra

description: Riverina Gate & Fencing Solutions supplies and installs gates and fencing in Wagga Wagga. Saturday appointments are available by arrangement.

highlights: Rural sheds, barns and industrial sheds
Erection and concrete slab can be arranged
Colour chart and sheeting guide online

highlights: Outdoor learning spaces and community parks
Aged care and higher education projects

highlights: Lovells GVM/GCM and Fulcrum suspension upgrades
RV servicing and vintage car repairs

highlights: Servicing for all makes and models

Valvoline, Ryco, NGK and Bendix parts

The team services and repairs motorbikes as well, listing itself as a Harley-Davidson specialist.

highlights: Tyre fitting, rotation and puncture repairs
Online booking, Zip Pay and Afterpay

24/7 towing with seven tilt tray trucks

highlights: Custom ute tray design and fabrication

Glass for tractors, buses and excavators

Western Star, MAN and Dennis Eagle support

High roller door access for caravans and boats

Cooking oil and motor oil recycling

Home, office, factory, farm and vehicle work

KIN restaurant, lunch Thursday to Sunday
Bonnie pizza, lunch Wednesday to Sunday

highlights: Reserved seated tastings can be booked

Quartz Cuisine cafe on site, 9am to 4pm daily
Giant chess set and lawn games

Vineyard Kitchen first Saturday of each month
Live music on the first Saturday of the month
Historic winery on the Murray River

Group bookings preferred for 10 or more

highlights: Fortified wine and single malt whisky tastings together
